articles.body: Skywatch: An Offline-First, Voice-First Stargazing PWA That Keeps the Screen the Shortest Part of Your Night This is an official submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge: Week 1 & 2 ("Touch Grass") , targeting the **Overall Winner * and Best Use of Gemma categories.* 🌌 The Problem: Stargazing Apps Keep Your Face Buried in Blue Light Most stargazing apps are interactive planetarium simulators. They expect you to hold a brightly glowing screen up to the sky, pinch-to-zoom across thousands of catalog items, and continuously interact with the display. There's just one problem: it takes 20 to 30 minutes for human eyes to produce rhodopsin and adapt to dark skies . Every time you look down at a mobile UI, you reset your dark adaptation.

articles.body: Long time since an update here - I've been kept busy by various personal things, so involvement on this project has been lower than usual, but I should be getting more towards normal now. While I've done a few other things for the db engine, the binary row representation is the most relevant. Binary rows Basically as said in previous posts, a data page will store a row/record as a contiguous chunk of bytes. Since the rows are variable length, we need to have an encoding for them as well. At its core, the format is compact and pretty clearly organized. We start with a header of course, then we have all the integers (fixed size), then a null bitmap then the string section (which will be variable length).

articles.title: AI Search Can't See Your Site? The 5-Minute robots.txt Check
articles.excerpt: Originally published on DigiHustle. Something odd is happening on the web right now. AI assistants answer more shopping and research questions every month, but websites are blocking the bots that feed…
articles.body: Originally published on DigiHustle . Something odd is happening on the web right now. AI assistants answer more shopping and research questions every month, but websites are blocking the bots that feed those answers at a record pace. New numbers tell the story. Sites on Cloudflare's network denied 13.47% of AI bot requests in the third quarter of 2026, up from 5.98% a year earlier, according to Cloudflare Radar data analyzed by TechnologyChecker.io and reported October 9. A separate snapshot of 4,242 robots.txt files found sites block GPTBot 1.6 times for every site that allows it. Meanwhile the crawlers keep knocking: search-triggered AI crawl requests nearly doubled from 6.51% of AI crawl activity in Q2 to 11.92% in Q3. Read that twice. AI systems want to read your site more than ever.

articles.body: Originally published as a Fonix.AI practical guide by AntEngage. This republication uses the same guide content. An answered call is only the beginning AI calling software answers or places telephone calls, understands the caller's request and helps execute a defined business workflow. To be useful, it needs more than a convincing voice: it must retrieve the right information, record the outcome and hand over to a person when the request goes beyond its scope. For an Indian business, a practical starting point is inbound enquiries or follow-up with people who requested contact. The goal might be a qualified enquiry, a confirmed callback or a booked appointment. Choose one of those outcomes before choosing a script, a call volume or a software plan.

articles.title: The quote you sent last week is still waiting for you
articles.excerpt: Think about the last quote you sent. A price, a scope, a polite sign off. Then what happened? If the answer is "nothing, so I assumed they went elsewhere," you are in good company. For many small busi…
articles.body: Think about the last quote you sent. A price, a scope, a polite sign off. Then what happened? If the answer is "nothing, so I assumed they went elsewhere," you are in good company. For many small businesses, the quote is where the process stops being a process. The work to win it was done. The work to follow it up depends on someone remembering. Silence is not a no A person who goes quiet after a quote is usually not rejecting you. They got busy, they showed it to a partner, or they are waiting for one more number before they can decide. Your quote is sitting in an inbox between a hundred other things. Most lost quotes are not lost to a competitor. They are lost to a gap where nobody asked. Why the follow up does not happen It is not laziness. It is that the follow up has no trigger.

articles.title: GPT-6's Intelligent UI: The Business Tasks We'd Actually Trust It With
articles.excerpt: Originally published on DigiHustle. On October 7, OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 with something it calls Intelligent UI. The short version: ChatGPT can now generate interactive interfaces inside the chat — c…
articles.body: Originally published on DigiHustle . ChatGPT Stopped Answering Questions and Started Building Tools On October 7, OpenAI rolled out GPT-6 with something it calls Intelligent UI. The short version: ChatGPT can now generate interactive interfaces inside the chat — calculators, bill splitters, comparison charts, adjustable diagrams, checklists — instead of just text. Paid users (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise) got it first with a model called GPT-6 Sol. Free and Go users were scheduled to get GPT-6 Luna from October 8. The mechanism is what makes it interesting. OpenAI built a library of native, streamable components plus a compiler that assembles the interface while the model is still generating its answer. Parts of the UI appear before the full response finishes.

articles.body: A crew annotated image showing where the Artemis II team observed impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon. | Image: NASA If you thought you'd seen all there is to see from the Artemis II mission , you're wrong. This week NASA posted over 800GB worth of science data, images, and videos on the Artemis II: Sights & Sounds of Science site. The archive includes over 11,000 photos and videos, over 8.5 hours of audio, and crew-annotated images, such as the one marking where they saw impact flashes on the dark side of the Moon. Together, they offer an unprecedented view inside a historic space mission. One of the more exciting reveals was footage of the Artemis II team telling the ground team back in Houston about its observation of impact flashes.

articles.body: NASA’s Freedom 250 F-5 team, including NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, performs a flyover during the national anthem at an NFL game between the Cleveland Browns and the Carolina Panthers at Huntington Bank Field, Sept. 27, 2026, in Cleveland. Credit: NASA/Jordan Cochran As part of the agency’s Inspiration Tour flyover, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman will pilot one of three F-5 fighter jets to kick off the New York Jets vs. Cleveland Browns game in East Rutherford, New Jersey, on Sunday, Oct. 11. articles.excerpt: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that…
articles.body: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested an executive at a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity. The New York Times reported today that the FBI has arrested a Canadian man in Pennsylvania on suspicion of assisting ShinyHunters. The Times story did not identify the man, nor did a statement on Twitter/X about the arrest from FBI Director Kash Patel .
